prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1406; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for side impact collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver's side by a second vehicle while proceeding through on green. Claimant reports neck strain and is seeking medical evaluation. No attorney on file; claimant is handling the claim directly. Initial liability appears to favor insured, pending scene review.

Entry 2: Called claimant to confirm contact details and obtain recorded statement. Claimant describes slowing for the light, then impact from the cross-traffic vehicle. Reports pain in neck and stiffness since the collision. Advised claimant of the medical documentation needed and the process for submitting bills. Claimant agreed to send records.

Entry 3: Reviewed police report and photos from the scene. Damage to insured vehicle is concentrated on the driver's side door and quarter panel. Other driver cited for failure to yield on left turn. Witness statement on file supports the insured's account of the signal phase. Liability assessment updated to favor insured.

Entry 4: Received claimant's urgent care visit notes. Diagnosis is cervical strain with recommended rest, a soft collar, and a course of physical therapy. No fractures or imaging-confirmed injuries reported at this time. Claimant indicated pain is improving but still limits sleep and driving for extended periods. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect injury treatment.

Entry 5: Sent claimant a written update confirming receipt of medical records and outlining next steps, including the physical therapy authorization form. Reminded claimant that they may consult an attorney at any time and that the adjuster can answer questions about the claim process. Follow-up scheduled to review therapy progress and status of the property damage estimate.
